review_candidates.title: Systems Engineer
review_candidates.description: Summary/Objectives The Systems Engineer role focuses on delivering planned work (deployments, refreshes, upgrades, and migrations) and providing strong Tier 2-level support as needed. This role is responsible for executing planned technical work with a strong focus on quality, validation, and clean handoff. The engineer follows documented standards and change discipline, communicates scope, risks, and dependencies clearly, and produces thorough as-built documentation to support long-term maintainability. The role requires strong customer-facing communication, including clear status updates and the ability to explain technical outcomes in plain language, as well as close collaboration with senior and escalation engineers to ensure issues are escalated early, lessons learned are captured, and standards and checklists are continuously improved. Essential Functions Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Networking and firewall fundamentals Can configure and troubleshoot VLANs (access vs trunk), basic routing concepts, and subnetting (CIDR). Understands DHCP and DNS fundamentals and common failure modes (scope exhaustion, reservations, DNS misconfigs). Can implement and validate basic firewall changes: rule updates, outbound NAT, and simple port forwards (with safe testing). Understands VPN basics (site-to-site and/or remote access) and how to validate connectivity and expected traffic paths. Uses standard troubleshooting tools and methods (ping/traceroute, ipconfig/route, nslookup, log review) with structured isolation. Switching and wireless operational basics Can turn up and validate switches and access points using standard baselines and documentation. Understands PoE basics and can troubleshoot common issues for APs/phones (power budget, link negotiation, cabling). Can verify VLAN tagging across uplinks and diagnose common L2 issues (mis-tagged VLANs, loops, STP blocking, bad uplinks). Understands fundamental wireless concepts (SSID security, guest isolation, basic roaming/coverage considerations) and can triage client issues. Windows Server and Active Directory fundamentals Hands-on experience administering Windows endpoints and servers in production (remote access, services, event logs, patching). Understands AD basics (users/groups, OUs, basic GPO concepts) and how DNS integrates with domain authentication. Can troubleshoot common domain and workstation issues (login failures, DNS-related problems, permissions/share access). Understands backup fundamentals and can follow restore verification steps (file restore and/or VM restore workflow). Virtualization fundamentals (VMware and/or Hyper-V) Comfortable performing common VM tasks: create/modify VMs, snapshot/checkpoint concepts, resource allocation, and safe reboot procedures. Understands virtual networking basics (vSwitch/port groups) and can validate connectivity issues at the VM/host level. Understands basic storage/capacity concerns (datastore space, IOPS symptoms, snapshots growing) and can escalate appropriately. Can triage common virtualization incidents (host down, VM hung, storage full) and follow a structured recovery plan. Microsoft 365 fundamentals Comfortable navigating Microsoft 365 admin centers (M365, Exchange, Teams, SharePoint) for day-to-day admin troubleshooting. Understands identity basics (MFA concepts; awareness of Conditional Access) and knows when to escalate high-risk identity changes. Can perform basic Exchange Online troubleshooting (mail flow checks, message trace, client connectivity triage). Can triage common Teams/SharePoint/OneDrive issues (permissions, sync problems, service health awareness). In-office staging/build/testing (hands-on) Can rack/stack devices, label, patch, and validate uplinks and connectivity in a staging environment. Comfortable with console access when needed (serial/USB) and initial device turn-up (mgmt IP, credentials, SSH). Applies standard baseline configs, updates firmware as directed, and documents outcomes. Validates functionality using a checklist (connectivity, VLANs, VPN, wireless, failover where applicable) and records results. Tooling and process fundamentals Works effectively in a ticketing system: clear updates, time entry, and complete technical notes. Uses documentation systems to update as-builts, diagrams, IP/VLAN records, and configuration notes. Understands change management expectations: approvals, change windows, and post-change validation. Knows when to escalate and how to provide a strong handoff (what changed, what was tested, what remains). Work Environment This job operates primarily in a professional office environment. The role provides remote support into customer environments from our office and performs hands-on staging/build/testing of equipment in an office/lab setting. Onsite customer visits may be required based on contract scope. Physical Demands This position may require standing, bending, and lifting equipment during staging/build activities. Ability to lift and carry up to 40 lbs, and to rack/mount equipment with assistance as needed. Position Type/Expected Hours of Work Full-time. Typical schedule is Monday through Friday during business hours. Occasional evening/weekend work may be required for maintenance windows, cutovers, or urgent events. Light on-call rotation (typically once every few months). Travel Occasional onsite customer visits may be required for specific contracts, cutovers, or escalations. Required Education And Experience 5+ years of IT support/implementation experience (MSP experience preferred). Working knowledge of networking fundamentals and troubleshooting (VLANs, subnetting, DHCP/DNS). Experience implementing and supporting Windows Server environments and/or virtualization platforms. Familiarity with Microsoft 365 administration (core admin centers and basic troubleshooting). Strong documentation habits and ability to follow and maintain standards. Professional customer communication and teamwork mindset. U.S. citizenship required to support certain regulated customers and environments. Preferred Education And Experience Hands-on Sophos firewall experience (NAT, VPN, policy changes). Ruckus and/or Aruba switching/wireless experience. VMware and/or Hyper-V; Scale Computing a plus. PowerShell scripting/automation. Experience supporting Commercial and/or GCC/GCC High tenants. Work Authorization/Security Clearance (if applicable) U.S. citizenship required to support certain regulated customers and environments. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. With easy access to 765,000 acres of public land, Winter Park is home to endless adventures. Whether you are looking to have your first taste of a winter season or to build a long-term career, we have something for everyone. Perks & Benefits: Free season pass to Winter Park and all Alterra Resorts Discounted friends & family tickets Medical, dental, vision, life, paid parental leave and more for eligible employees 401(k) plan with 100% company match - up to 4% Mental health resources for all employees Food & beverage and retail discounts Onsite employee childcare based on availability Discounted equipment rentals, pro-deals, and more ATTN: To be considered, resume and cover letter are required. POSITION SUMMARY: The IT Systems Administrator (ITSA) is a senior technical contributor responsible for the design, implementation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and support of Winter Park Resort’s IT infrastructure, including servers, cloud services, identity systems, point-of-sale platforms, mobile devices, telecommunications, storage, and related technologies. Working under the direction of the Sr. Infrastructure Manager and in partnership with the IT Operations Manager, the ITSA provides advanced operational support, serves as an escalation resource for complex technical issues, and participates in local and Enterprise-level projects and initiatives. The role requires strong technical expertise, independent judgment, excellent customer service, and the ability to balance day-to-day operations with strategic technology initiatives. The ITSA follows all Winter Park Resort, Alterra, and applicable regulatory policies and procedures. WAGE: The base salary pay range below represents the low and high end of Winter Park Resorts' salary pay range for this position. Actual pay will vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors including but not limited to experience, education, training, location, merit system, quantity or quality of production, responsibilities, and regular and/or necessary travel. The range listed is just one component of Winter Park Resorts' total compensation package for employees. Other rewards may include many region-specific benefits. Salary pay range: $82,000 - $86,000 ESSENTIAL DUTIES: Infrastructure Administration & Support Administer, maintain, monitor, and support assigned technology platforms, including servers, networking, wireless, storage, backup, telecommunications, cloud, and SaaS/IaaS solutions. Serve as a subject matter expert for designated infrastructure systems and manage their lifecycle. Provide advanced troubleshooting and resolution of incidents and service requests. Participate in on-call rotations and support a 24/7 resort operation. Maintain compliance with ITIL-based service management processes and ticketing standards. Automation & Technical Development Develop, maintain, review, and troubleshoot PowerShell scripts and automation solutions. Participate in proof-of-concept testing, system evaluations, and technology recommendations. Support implementation of new technologies, upgrades, and infrastructure improvements. Collaboration & Documentation Work closely with IT leadership, resort departments, Enterprise IT teams, and vendors. Maintain thorough system documentation, inventory records, operational procedures, and technical standards. Participate in Enterprise working groups and project teams supporting resort and corporate initiatives. Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders. Operational Expectations Work a standard schedule while maintaining flexibility for evenings, weekends, holidays, maintenance windows, and emergency support. Follow all company policies, standards, security requirements, and operational procedures. Perform additional duties as assigned. EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE: Education High School Diploma or equivalent required. Degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, or related field preferred; equivalent experience accepted. Experience Minimum 5 years of experience installing, maintaining, and supporting computer systems and software. Minimum 3 years of experience in systems administration, server infrastructure, or network administration. Demonstrated ability to independently troubleshoot complex technical issues in high-availability environments. QUALIFICATIONS & TECHNICAL SKILLS: Valid Colorado Driver’s License required. Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving abilities. Experience with Microsoft Windows, Windows Server, Active Directory, Group Policy, Entra ID, and Microsoft 365. Working knowledge of PowerShell scripting and automation. Experience with virtualization technologies such as VMware, Nutanix, or Hyper-V. Familiarity with Linux/Unix systems preferred. Experience supporting mobile devices (iOS, Android, Windows). Knowledge of network technologies including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, Wi-Fi, switching, and routing. Experience with storage technologies (NAS/SAN), VoIP systems, and low-voltage cabling. Familiarity with cloud platforms, SaaS applications, enterprise server systems, and infrastructure monitoring tools. Experience with point-of-sale systems, PCI compliance, and SOX controls preferred. TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS: Primary work location is Winter Park, Colorado. Occasional travel to Denver-area facilities, Alterra resorts, and other business locations may be required. WORK ENVIRONMENT & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: Ability to lift and move up to 40 pounds with assistance. Ability to travel throughout resort properties via walking, driving, skiing/riding, snowmobile, or ATV as needed. Ability to work indoors and outdoors in high-altitude mountain environments. Manual dexterity and visual/auditory acuity required for operation of computers, mobile devices, and technical equipment. Ability to sit, stand, walk, bend, kneel, reach, and carry equipment for extended periods as required. AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER: Winter Park Resort is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is dedicated to the principles of equal employment opportunity in any term, condition, or privilege of employment. Application Deadline: Recruiting timelines vary by position, however, all Winter Park Resort positions accept applications for a minimum of 3 business days from the posting date listed above. Manage core enterprise services, including Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, NPS, and PKI. Oversee system monitoring, logging, patch management, backups, disaster recovery, and endpoint security. Lead complex troubleshooting efforts involving servers, virtualization, networking, authentication, and application performance. Manage vulnerability remediation, IAVAs, STIG compliance, security scanning, and patching in accordance with DoD requirements. Work with cybersecurity teams to implement security controls, address findings, and support RMF and ATO activities. Develop and maintain technical documentation, SOPs, system configurations, network diagrams, and recovery procedures. Lead system integration, testing, and deployment activities to meet operational and cybersecurity requirements. Mentor junior personnel, review configurations, and provide technical guidance. Minimum Secret to start. Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field with 12+ years of relevant experience. Additional experience may substitute for a degree. Minimum of 7 years of Windows systems administration experience, including 3 years in a senior or technical lead role. Minimum of 5 years of experience with Active Directory, DNS, Group Policy, and core Windows enterprise services. Active Top Secret/SCI security clearance or current Secret security clearance with the ability to obtain a TS/SCI security clearance within 365 days from hire date. Strong experience with Microsoft Hyper-V, virtual machines, clustering, storage, and Windows Server 2022/2025. Working knowledge networking, including TCP/IP, VLANs, routing, and firewalls. Experience with PowerShell scripting, automation, and Windows command-line tools. Experience supporting monitoring, logging, patch management, backup, and disaster recovery solutions. Hands-on experience with vulnerability scanning, IAVA remediation, STIG compliance, and system hardening. Working knowledge of DoD cybersecurity requirements, including NIST SP 800-53, RMF, and security configuration standards. Ability to troubleshoot complex infrastructure issues, support system integration, and maintain technical documentation and SOPs. Demonstrated ability to lead technical efforts, mentor junior administrators, work across engineering teams, and independently resolve technical challenges. Experience with data center installations, including rack-and-stack, cabling, power, and out-of-band management. Experience integrating Windows and Linux systems with Cisco networking, firewalls, and secure remote access. Experience supporting Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), System Acceptance Testing (SAT), and technical design reviews. Experience leading infrastructure deployments, developing installation procedures, and improving system administration processes.
